value:
A DECLARED-TYPE DIVERGENCE BETWEEN TWO TUs THAT ARE BOTH ALREADY 100% MATCHED IS NOT A DEFECT - IT IS PROOF THAT THE SHIPPED SOURCE CARRIED TWO DIFFERENT SPELLINGS, AND HARMONIZING IT CAN ONLY REGRESS. The shim law established that a consumer's own bytes, not the definition, decide its declaration. The mechanical consequence for a defect TABLE is stronger than that law states, and it is FREE: for every row, look up each declaring TU's matched_functions_percent in build/GUNE5D/report.json. A TU at 100% has, by construction, no function whose codegen could be improved by any declaration change, so its spelling is correct-as-shipped and is a VETO on that side. When TWO OR MORE sides of one row are at 100% AND they disagree with each other, the row is a PROVEN SHIP-SHIPPED DIVERGENCE with no single truth to harmonize toward, and it must be struck from the defect list rather than worked.

MEASURED ON THE WHOLE TABLE, cost zero builds. Of the 91 object CONFLICT rows remaining after this pass, 13 have two-or-more mutually disagreeing EXACT sides: gErrorCode (ml_mem.c `int` and ml_error.c `s32`, both 100%), lbl_80343F0C (mb_window.c `s32`, pb_winglobals.c `u32`), lbl_802A4B30 (mb_objects.c `s32`, mb_main.c `u32`), lbl_80344DA8 (main.c `u32`, mb_main.c `u8`), lbl_803441B0/B4/B8 (anim_play.c `f32*`, anim.c `u32`), lbl_80344EAC/EB0/EB4/EBC/ECC (mb_tree.c `MBTreeNode*`, mb_objects.c `void*`, pb_tree.cpp `PBTREENODE*`), and gWinGlobals - whose 14 declaring TUs include five separate 100%-matched TUs each naming the same address a DIFFERENT pointer type (MBStructGlobals*, MBWinGlobals*, MLErrorWinGlobals*, PbWGGlobals*, and the header's PBWINGLOBALS*). gWinGlobals is the decisive specimen: it is a single 4-byte .sbss word that the retail sources genuinely viewed through a dozen unrelated per-subsystem window-globals types, so a 14-way 'conflict' that looks like the table's worst row is in fact its most conclusively CLOSED one. Two further rows (_stack_addr, _stack_end) have their only non-header side in the 100%-matched OSThread.c and are equally closed. So 15 of 91 rows - one in six - are not work items at all.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A LAW RATHER THAN A NOTE. The externcheck table's severity column is computed purely from declared-type text and is therefore blind to match state; read literally it commands an edit on rows where an edit is provably harmful, and the natural 'fix the odd one out' instinct on a row like gWinGlobals or lbl_803441B0 points straight at a 100%-matched TU. Applying this screen FIRST also reorders the remaining work usefully: after removing the 15 closed rows and the rows blocked by other fleets' claims, what is left splits into 11 rows carrying exactly one EXACT anchor plus a NonMatching outlier - the highest-confidence queue, because the anchor supplies a spelling that is known-right for at least one TU and the outlier is the only side that can move - and 16 all-NonMatching rows where no side is privileged and target-asm access widths must be read before touching anything. CAUTION, and the boundary: TU-level match state is a SUFFICIENT veto, never a necessary one. A NonMatching TU's declaration may still be correct-as-shipped, since only the functions that actually reference the symbol are evidence; the shim law's own confirmation case (newcam.c DebugCamControlInputs byte-exact inside a NonMatching TU) is exactly that situation. So this screen closes rows, it does not open them - never read 'this side is NonMatching' as licence to change it.
